description:
Construction of a two-storey front/side extension and construction of first floor rear extension. Installation of two roof lights to front roof slope. Alterations to fenestration at front elevation
comprising installation of two bay windows.
decision_conditions:
<p class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:auto;mso-margin-bottom-alt:auto;
line-height:normal"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;,serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-fareast-language:EN-GB">The
two-storey side extension with a gabled roof and the alterations to the
existing double-storey bay windows by virtue of the design, overall bulk and height
would be out of keeping with the character of the host property, the attached
semi, and the relevant parade of dwellings along Lodge Villa. &nbsp;The proposals are visually dominant which
conflicts with the character and design of the host property and the street
setting, and would set an undesirable precedence for future developments within
the locality. The development would be contrary to policies 53 of the Waltham
Forest Local Plan LP1 (2024) and Supplementary Planning Documents National
Design Guide (2021) and &nbsp;Residential
Extensions and Alterations'(2010).<o:p></o:p></span></p><p>

</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:auto;mso-margin-bottom-alt:auto;
line-height:normal"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;,serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-fareast-language:EN-GB">The
proposed flat roofed two-storey rear extension would be of a poor appearance
and design. It would appear as a large, bulky addition when viewed from the
rear and would not appear subservient to the host building or be appropriate
for the setting of a listed building. The proposals would be contrary to
policies 53, 70 and 71 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan LP1 (2024) and Supplementary
Planning Documents National Design Guide (2021) and &nbsp;Residential Extensions and Alterations'(2010).<o:p></o:p></span></p>
